deck: Table Rock this morning: 909.37 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Warm the hands, not the water.
play.body: Fish the warmest part of the afternoon on the lake. Fish first light on the trout water. Different climates.

season.name: Winter trout
season.why: Table Rock gets quiet and vertical. Taneycomo becomes the reason you came. This is Johnny Morris water — cold, clear, and honest.
tips: Spoon or ice jig over 30–50 feet on Table Rock if you must. Most people shouldn't.
Taneycomo is the trip: midges, eggs, pink worms, tiny jigs, 2-pound test.
Generation still rules. A winter blowdown is a drift day.
Felt soles and a staff if you wad. The rocks don't care that you're on vacation.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 909.65 early in the week to 909.37 this morning — about 0.28 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: At ~909.4 ft the lake is more than 5.6 ft below full pool. Exposed shoreline, shallow coves, and longer walks at some ramps are the norm — navigate carefully in the James, Kings, and Long Creek arms where hazards sit closer to the surface.

Surface water has cooled into the upper 50s with gin-clear clarity. Bass are hitting topwaters and soft plastics in low light before transitioning to jigs, live bait, drop-shot, or tubes around long points, gravel flats dropping into 20–40 ft, and offshore structure. Walleye and crappie continue to produce around brush piles and points. In this clear, cooling water, precise natural presentations win the day as fish feed heavily ahead of winter.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad. Do not guess the generators.

body: This cold tailwater remains one of the most reliable trout fisheries thanks to consistent MDC stocking and cold releases from the bottom of Table Rock Dam. Generation is the primary tactic book: low or no generation (as scheduled for much of today) allows lighter rigs, wading, or indicator fishing in seams and soft water; stronger flows demand added weight, drifting the current breaks, and 2–4 lb test.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics or scented/natural baits allowed. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, or other soft plastics/scented baits for water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in many areas. Recent reports show solid numbers of rainbows with increasing brown trout activity in the upper stretches on marabou jigs, midges, scuds, small streamers, and eggs. Water clarity is generally excellent. Always call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA generation schedule before heading out and stay clear of the closed zone below the dam.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
